note: Visual-composition outcome corpus for the quiet dashboard (FIX-DS-06.01, finding DS-06/XD-13). Two judged layers are SEPARATE by design: routing/constraint/provenance correctness is judged deterministically on artifacts here; the VISUAL outcome is judged by an independent render rubric against the actual render at the same viewport and content — and that live model/render eval is a SEPARATE authorized execution batch after implementation, which no fixture task imitates. A mechanical PASS never substitutes for composition judgement, a claimed screenshot must EXIST as a decodable file (a mention is not a file), an offline/no-keys route reports NOT_RUN and proposes no install, and 100% structural PASS is never phrased as a proven design improvement — quality comparison runs with identical inputs, model budget and viewports, blind variant order and repeated samples, recording failures/cost/time, and stays UNMEASURED until that run.

prompt.text: Explore composition variants for an already-correct quiet dashboard (tokens clean, hierarchy right). Identity-preserving: a correct render is NOT obliged to change — record kept/changed per region with a reason into exploration-log.md; zero changes with reasons is a valid outcome.

Build the quiet dashboard type spec constrained to the SYSTEM font stack and ONE family total: hierarchy must come from size/weight/spacing only. Write type-spec.md and record any fault where hierarchy needed a second family (fault, not a style name).

Design the dense data table region of the quiet dashboard (40 rows visible, 8 columns) at viewport 1440x900 with the SAME content fixture both arms use. Write table-spec.md naming row height, alignment per column type, and the faults found on the actual render — a fault names a region and what is wrong, never only a token/style name.

Review the quiet dashboard WITHOUT any screenshot or render available: every claim that needs the render is marked NOT_RUN (what it would take), and no screenshot path is cited as existing. Write render-review.md.

Produce a NATIVE mobile mockup spec for the dashboard's phone companion (SwiftUI semantics, no served HTML): platform conventions decide, web-only checks are marked N/A with the reason. Write native-spec.md.

outcome.name: web-only checks are N/A with reason

prompt.text: The Figma MCP and Chrome tooling are UNAVAILABLE in this environment. Route the quiet-dashboard review accordingly: name what each absent tool would have verified, mark those checks NOT_RUN, and do NOT propose installing anything. Write tooling-note.md.

outcome.name: absent tools named, no install proposed
